newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Briton ends 20,000 km cycle to Australia.
newsitem.headline: Briton ends 20,000 km cycle to Australia.

text.p: A British cyclist on Saturday ended a 20,000 km (12,000 mile) charity ride from England to Australia.
Tom Fremantle rode from Swanbourne in Buckinghamshire, some 30 miles (50 km) north of London to the suburb of Swanbourne in the far-west Australian city of Perth.
"It was a magical feeling," Fremantle said in a television interview.
"I've been waiting for 16 months to see the Swanbourne sign and so it was absolutely terrific."
Fremantle is the great, great, great grandnephew of British admiral Sir Charles Fremantle, who sailed from England to Australia's west coast in 1829.
The historic port city of Fremantle, just south of Perth and home to the America's Cup yachting challenge in the mid-1980s, was named after the admiral.
Tom Fremantle, who left home in February, 1996, raised about A$40,000 (US$30,000) for a British hospital.
